title: G. Simons and Diophantus Equation
statement:
Simons has given you two integers $$n$$ and $$m$$.

Count the number of ordered tuples $$(i, j, k)$$, such that:

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows.

The only line contains two integers $$n$$ and $$m$$ ($$1$\leq n\leq 10^9$$$, $$1$\leq m\leq 3\cdot 10^5$$$) — the given integers.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $$m$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$3\cdot10^5$$.

For each test case, output a single integer — the number of ordered tuples $$(i,j,k)$$ that satisfy the condition.

In the first test case, there are $$18$$ tuples that satisfy the conditions. For example:
input: Input Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The only line contains two integers $$n$$ and $$m$$ ($$1$\leq n\leq 10^9$$$, $$1$\leq m\leq 3\cdot 10^5$$$) — the given integers. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$m$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$3\cdot10^5$$.
output: Output For each test case, output a single integer — the number of ordered tuples $$(i,j,k)$$ that satisfy the condition.
